problems.title: Simplify a quotient of powers
problems.question: Calculate (3⁵·6⁸)/(9⁶·4⁴).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: Cancel the powers of 2. The remaining power of 3 is 3^(5+8−12)=3.

problems.title: Two roots of an absolute-value equation
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |2x−3|=11.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: The roots are 7 and −4. Their sum is 3.

problems.title: A common factor vanishes
problems.question: Evaluate x³+2x²y−4x−8y when x=−2y.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: The second factor is zero, so the whole expression is zero.

problems.title: Circumdiameter from a thirty-degree angle
problems.question: A triangle has A=30° and BC=12. Find its circumcircle diameter.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: Since sin30°=1/2, 12=R, giving diameter 2R=24.

problems.title: Arcs cut by intersecting chords
problems.question: Two lines meet inside a circle at 50°. The arcs inside that angle and its vertical angle differ by 10°. Find the larger arc.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Interior chord angle = half the sum of its intercepted arcs.
steps: The two arcs sum to 100°. Solve u+v=100°,u−v=10° to get u=55°,v=45°.

problems.title: Recover an added observation from a mean
problems.question: Seven numbers average 10. Adding an eighth makes the average 12. Find the added number.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: The old sum is 70 and new sum 96. The added number is 96−70=26.

problems.title: Clock hands at 19:22
problems.question: Find the smaller clock-hand angle at 19:22.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: The angles are 221° and 132°. Their difference is 89°, already below 180°.

problems.title: Inverse-proportional angles
problems.question: Triangle angles are inversely proportional to 3,4,6. Find largest minus smallest.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: Nine parts total 180°, so one part is 20°. The angles are 80°,60°,40°, giving a difference of 40°.

problems.title: Intersecting circles and a common external tangent
problems.question: Two circles meet at A,B and have common external tangent CD. BCD=30°,BDC=20°, and CAD<CBD. Find CAD.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Tangent-chord theorem: the angle between a tangent and chord equals the angle subtended in the alternate segment.
steps: Triangle BCD gives CBD=180°−30°−20°=130°. Transfer the two tangent-chord angles through A using the two circles: the smaller angle CAD is 30°+20°=50°.
The other intersection arrangement swaps the smaller and larger angles. The condition CAD<CBD selects 50°, consistent with CBD=130°.

problems.title: Equation through two points
problems.question: Find the line through (4,−7) and (−2,5).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: m=12/(−6)=−2. Substitute (4,−7): −7=−8+b, so b=1. The other point checks: −2(−2)+1=5.

problems.title: Compare two divisor counts
problems.question: a=7·11³·13⁴ and b=2³·3⁴·5⁷. By what percent is a’s divisor count less than b’s?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Divisor count $=\prod(e_i+1)$; percent decrease uses the larger count as its denominator.

problems.title: A finite geometric series
problems.question: Calculate 1+1/2+(1/2)²+…+(1/2)¹².
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.

problems.title: Coefficient sum of a polynomial
problems.question: Find the sum of coefficients after expanding (2a+b)²+(a−3b)².
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: The sum of coefficients of P(a,b) is $P(1,1)$.

problems.title: Right-triangle perimeter from two radii
problems.question: A right triangle has circumradius 10 and inradius 4. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: c=20. Then a+b=2r+c=28, so perimeter=28+20=48.

problems.title: An angle bisector from an obtuse isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has B=140°. The distance from C to line AB is 3. Find C-bisector CK.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Base angles are 20°; in triangle CKB the angle at K is $180°-140°-10°=30°$.
steps: Let H be the perpendicular foot from C to line AB. Since K,H lie on that line, CH=CK sin30°=CK/2.
Thus CK=2×3=6. This uses the distance to the full line, so an external altitude foot is allowed.

problems.title: Symmetry axis of an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC, A=(3,1),C=(7,1). Find the line containing the altitude from B.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: An isosceles triangle’s apex altitude is the perpendicular bisector of its base.
steps: The base is horizontal, with midpoint (5,1). Its perpendicular bisector is the vertical line x=5.

problems.title: A circle touching four lines
problems.question: A circle touches y=6,y=2,x=1,x=−3. Find its centre.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Equal distances to two parallel lines place the centre on their midway line.
steps: The midpoint y coordinate is (6+2)/2=4 and x coordinate (1−3)/2=−1. Both pairs are distance 4 apart, giving consistent radius 2.

problems.title: A linear-function equation
problems.question: Solve f(x+4)=f(2x−1)+5 for f(t)=5t+1.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.

problems.title: A forbidden triangle perimeter
problems.question: Two triangle sides are 6,10. Which listed perimeter 19,21,25,29,30,31 is impossible?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: The third side c satisfies $|10-6|<c<10+6$, so $20<P=16+c<32$.
steps: Only 19 lies outside this open interval. The others correspond to third sides strictly between 4 and 16.

problems.title: Angle between a right-triangle median and altitude
problems.question: In a right triangle, the altitude and median to the hypotenuse form 10°. Find its smallest angle.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: If an acute angle is α, the two lines from the right vertex form $|90°-2\alpha|$.
steps: To see the formula, put the right vertex at the origin and the legs along the axes. The median direction makes α with one axis, while the altitude direction makes 90°−α.
Thus |90°−2α|=10°, giving α=40° or 50°. These are the two acute angles of the same shape; the smaller is 40°.

problems.title: A specified root constrains a parameter
problems.question: x=4 solves a²−3a−ax−|2x²−24|=0. Find the greatest possible a.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: a²−7a−|32−24|=a²−7a−8=(a−8)(a+1)=0. The possible values are 8 and −1, so the greatest is 8.

problems.title: A reflected point and a parallel line
problems.question: Find the line parallel to y=4x−7 through the x-axis reflection of (−3,5).
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: Write y=4x+b. Substitution gives −5=−12+b, so b=7.

problems.title: Four solution pairs force coincident lines
problems.question: For which listed n can 2x−1=nx+5y and 3x−15y=3 have four distinct solution pairs?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Two linear equations have at most one common point unless their lines coincide.
steps: The second simplifies to x−5y=1. The first is (2−n)x−5y=1.
They coincide exactly when 2−n=1, so n=1. Then there are infinitely many pairs, including four distinct pairs.

problems.title: A symmetric right triangle on a hypotenuse
problems.question: ABC is right at C. On hypotenuse AB, construct isosceles right AOB with right angle O on the opposite side from C. Find BCO:ACO.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
formulas: Both C and O lie on the circle with diameter AB. Equal chords AO,BO subtend equal angles at C.
steps: The isosceles right construction gives AO=BO, so angles ACO and BCO are equal. Together they make ACB=90°, hence each is 45°. Their ratio is 1:1.

problems.title: Altitude intersections on the circumcircle
problems.question: In an acute triangle, altitudes from A,B,C meet the circumcircle again at A₁,B₁,C₁. If A=60°, find C₁A₁B₁.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or theorem, then substitute and verify the result.
steps: The arcs CB₁ and BC₁ adjacent to arc BC have measures 180°−2C and 180°−2B, by perpendicularity and the inscribed-angle theorem. Arc BC through A₁ is 2A.
Their total is 4A, so the opposite arc C₁B₁ measures 360°−4A. Halving gives 180°−2A=60°.
